cases.title: RahmaCare
cases.headline: smart healthcare in the family's hands
cases.summary: A complete Flutter app for managing a family's health with AI: instant triage, close follow-up, and an experience built around the person before the screen.
cases.heroAlt: The general ledger in RahmaCare: entries in sequence, each with a serial number and a hash

gallery.cap: The home screen — every family member's file in a single card

gallery.alt: The general ledger: a verifiable record
gallery.cap: The general ledger — every action is sequenced and hashed, so nothing changes quietly

challenge.p: A single family manages appointments, medicines and reports for several people across paper, WhatsApp messages and the mother's memory. And in health relief specifically, polished numbers are everywhere with no traceable source.
points: A health record per person with different permissions inside the same family
An AI assistant that reads the case and warns early — without making the medical decision
No number published on the platform without a source that can be traced
Full accessibility: keyboard, screen reader, and a path for deaf users

approach.t: A health file for the whole family
approach.d: A record per person with their appointments, medicines and reports, with different view permissions per role inside the family. The father sees his own, the mother sees the children, the doctor sees only what was granted.

approach.t: An assistant that reads the case, not just answers
approach.d: An AI layer summarises the indicators and warns early, while the medical decision stays human. Every alert carries its source: which reading, which date, and which threshold it crossed.

approach.t: A ledger that cannot change quietly
approach.d: Every action — appointment, medicine, aid — is recorded with a serial number and a hash chained to the one before it. The beneficiary sees who viewed their file and when, and consent is explicit and revocable.

cases.solution: A Flutter app with one codebase for iOS and Android, over a Firebase backend, with an AI layer that works inside the task flow rather than in a side panel. Accessibility is not an add-on: the full path is tested with a screen reader, with a dedicated path for deaf and non-speaking users.

impact.label: platforms from one codebase
of published numbers tied to a source
general ledger, sequenced and hashed
WCAG 2.1 accessibility across the app

notes.b: A health file for the whole family
notes.s: A record per person with appointments, medicines and reports, with different view permissions per role.

notes.b: An assistant that reads the case
notes.s: An AI layer summarises indicators and warns early, while the medical decision stays human.
Keyboard, screen reader and a full path for deaf users — because someone who cannot use the product was not built for.

cases.title: Jameel Store
cases.headline: a luxury store with a world-class shopping experience
cases.summary: From browsing to payment in one flow that never breaks — a Flutter interface over a Firebase backend, designed Arabic-first.
cases.heroAlt: The Jameel Store interface: a product page and a cart, rendered Arabic-first

gallery.cap: Product page and cart — numbers, prices and dates are Arabic by origin

challenge.p: Arabic stores are usually built on a Latin template and then flipped. The result: reversed prices, strange dates, and a cart that is lost when the network drops — and it does drop.
points: One flow from browsing to payment that does not break at any step
Native Arabic rendering: direction, numerals, prices and dates
A cart preserved across sessions and devices, syncing when the network returns
Smooth scrolling on long lists on mid-range devices

approach.d: The interface was designed in Figma on an Arabic-first component system, then carried into Flutter with a matching component library — so there are no surprises between design and build.

approach.t: A cart that is never lost
approach.d: Cart state is stored locally and synced with Firebase when the network returns. The user closes the app in a lift and opens it in the car to find the cart exactly as they left it.
Lazy list building and multi-size images, so scrolling stays smooth on mid-range devices — not only on the newest phone.

cases.solution: A Flutter app with one codebase, a Firebase backend for the catalogue and orders, and a component library taken from the Figma file itself. Direction, numerals, prices and dates are all tuned for Arabic from the root — not flipped from a Latin template.

impact.label: purchase flow that never breaks
platforms from one codebase
native Arabic rendering from the root
a cart that works offline and syncs later

notes.b: A cart that is never lost
notes.s: Preserved across sessions and devices, syncing when the network returns.
Direction, numerals, prices and dates tuned for Arabic — not flipped from a Latin template.
Lazy building and multi-size images keep scrolling smooth on mid-range devices.

cases.title: Vibe OS 4.0
cases.headline: an operating system for the web, not just a website
cases.summary: Rebuilding the interface layer from zero: a design system of independent components and a glass surface that reads what is behind it, delivered as the base the group's products are built on.
cases.heroAlt: The Vibe OS 4.0 surface: independent glass windows, an in-task assistant, and an app dock

metric.honor: The base for Smart Accountant and the Academy

challenge.p: Every product in the group was rebuilding its own buttons, windows and tables. Any change to the identity meant redoing the work in four places, and AI was always a chat panel stuck to the side.
points: One component system where the whole identity changes from a single place
AI inside the task itself, not in a side panel
A live glass surface that stays readable in Arabic at AA contrast
A base the next products start from without a rebuild

approach.d: Every surface is built from documented components driven by central design tokens: colour, spacing, type, motion. Changing one value changes the identity in every product that consumes the system.
Help appears inside the field or table the user is working in and suggests the next step in context — instead of a separate chat window that interrupts the task.
Glass layers are tuned to measured contrast, with a fixed dark ground behind the text so transparency never turns into visual noise behind Arabic letterforms.

cases.solution: A full interface layer in TypeScript and React over a central design-token system, with independent components that carry their own state. It became the ground the Smart Accountant and Academy interfaces started from — the same buttons, the same tables, the same motion.

impact.label: design system feeding every product in the group
major versions, up to 4.0
products built on top of it
measured contrast on the glass surfaces

notes.s: Every surface is built from documented components, so the whole identity changes from one place.
Help appears inside the task itself instead of a separate chat panel.

notes.b: The base for what came next
notes.s: What was built here became the ground for the Smart Accountant and Academy interfaces.

cases.title: Smart Accountant
cases.headline: an IFRS accounting system, Arabic from the root
cases.summary: A complete double-entry accounting system built on IFRS that reads your invoices, proposes the balanced entry and closes the month with you — built to replace manual data entry, not the accountant.
cases.heroAlt: The Smart Accountant cockpit: revenue, expenses, net cash flow and the last balanced entry

facts.v: An Awalim product — live at clients in several countries

challenge.p: Most of what is sold in this region as an «accounting system» is a pretty interface over a spreadsheet: unbalanced entries pass, one client's data shows up for another, and Arabic is a translation laid over a Latin template.
points: No unbalanced entry passes — no in-between state, no fixing it later
Multi-tenant data isolation on three independent layers
Behaviour that changes entirely by country pack: currency, tax, zakat, weekend, end of service
Reading invoices with the camera and proposing a balanced entry for human approval

approach.d: A hierarchical chart of accounts, a ledger per account, upward balance aggregation with the correct sign, and posted journal entries with a full audit trail. The core was built and tested before any screen.
A permission guard on the route, a storage layer scoped to the entity, and row-level security policies inside PostgreSQL itself — defence in depth that does not rest on one layer.

approach.t: Scan the invoice, take the entry
approach.d: A document box reads photographs of invoices and receipts — uploaded or from the camera — extracts the fields and proposes a balanced entry. Approval is always human.
A financial health indicator, early alerts, a cash-flow forecast and «what if» simulation before the decision — built on the real numbers, not on estimates.

cases.solution: TypeScript end to end with contracts shared between client and server, PostgreSQL with Drizzle and exported reviewable migrations, schema validation on every request, and automated tests covering the critical accounting paths. The interface is natively right-to-left with tuned Arabic typography and tabular numerals.

impact.label: modules, from the general ledger to the decision room
country packs, each with full behaviour
data isolation layers
payroll and end-of-service to the standard

notes.b: No entry passes unless it balances
notes.s: A hierarchical chart of accounts, a ledger per account, and posted entries with a full audit trail.

notes.b: Scan the invoice, take the entry
notes.s: A document box reads the images and proposes a balanced entry for human approval.
A route guard, entity-scoped storage, and row policies inside the database itself.

cases.title: Maya
cases.headline: an identity where eastern heritage meets modernity
cases.summary: A complete visual identity for a perfume brand: mark, colour palette, Arabic and Latin typography, and an application system that runs from the bottle to the screen.
cases.heroAlt: The Maya identity: the mark and the hand-drawn Arabic name on the bottle

gallery.cap: Mark and name — tested on bottle, card and screen before approval

metric.standard: A mark that works at 1 cm

challenge.p: An identity that looks beautiful in a slide and then collapses on a three-centimetre bottle is not an identity. And an Arabic name set in an off-the-shelf typeface loses the joins between its letters at small sizes.
points: A mark that works at one centimetre on the bottle and full-screen at the same time
An Arabic name that keeps its letter joins at every size
A colour palette that holds the same on paper and on screen
A usage guide a designer and a print shop both understand

approach.t: A mark tested before it is approved
approach.d: The mark was tested on the bottle, the card and the screen at real sizes before approval — not on a slide. Anything that did not hold at one centimetre was redrawn.
The Arabic name was drawn by hand to keep its letter joins at small sizes, with a Latin cut that shares its rhythm without imitating it.

approach.t: A guide that can be executed
approach.d: Clear rules for spacing, backgrounds and forbidden uses, with files ready for print and for screen — not a slide deck forgotten in a month.

cases.solution: A complete identity: mark, colour palette, Arabic and Latin typography, and an application system running from the bottle to the screen, with an executable usage guide.

impact.label: smallest size at which the mark still reads
type systems, Arabic and Latin, on one rhythm
a palette tuned for paper and screen
executable, for designer and print shop

notes.b: A mark that works at one centimetre
notes.s: Tested on bottle, card and screen before approval — not on a slide.
The Arabic name was drawn by hand to keep its joins at small sizes.
Clear rules for spacing, backgrounds and forbidden uses — understood by designer and printer alike.

cases.title: Awalim Academy
cases.headline: a learning platform for the next generation of engineers
cases.summary: Tracks, real projects and code review — a platform built to teach engineering the way it is practised, not the way it is explained in a video.
cases.heroAlt: The Academy platform: the track project, its tasks with their states, and a code review written on the trainee's own code

gallery.cap: The track screen — the project, the code reviews and the tests in one place

challenge.p: Video series get watched and forgotten. An engineer learns by writing real code, having it reviewed line by line, and resubmitting — exactly as in a real team. The platform had to force that, not merely allow it.
points: A full track built around one project delivered at the end
Code review written on the trainee's own code
Tests from day one, before the feature
A published deliverable for the professional portfolio

approach.d: Every trainee builds one product across the whole track instead of scattered exercises that are forgotten. The platform tracks the project, not the lessons.

approach.t: Code review, not a model answer
approach.d: Written notes on the trainee's own code, then a resubmission — as it goes in a real team. There is no «model solution», because real solutions are many.
Training is not a revenue line — it is how we build the team we later hire, and how we keep our engineering standards alive. A large part of the Awalim team today came from the Academy.

cases.solution: A web platform where tracks are run as projects: a repository per trainee, written code reviews, and tests run on every submission. Four engineering tracks, each ending in a published product.

notes.s: Every trainee builds one product across the whole track instead of scattered exercises.

notes.b: Code review, not a model answer
notes.s: Written notes on the trainee's own code, then a resubmission — as it goes in a real team.
and {certifiedGraduates} finished a full track — a large part of today's Awalim team came from them.

cases.title: Automotive dashboard
cases.headline: instant reading in an environment that tolerates no hesitation
cases.summary: An interface study for driving: speed, energy and route in a single visual sequence, with absolute priority for safety over decoration.
cases.heroAlt: A dashboard: speed, energy and route in a three-level visual hierarchy

gallery.cap: The visual hierarchy — what must be seen in a fraction of a second comes first

challenge.p: A driver does not read the screen; they glance at it. Anything that takes more than a fraction of a second to understand is a hazard — and the visual decoration that looks superb in a dark room disappears under midday sun.
points: What must be seen in a fraction of a second, then what is read at a stop, then what is hidden
One colour that carries meaning — so when it changes the driver knows something really changed
Contrast measured under direct brightness, not on a desk monitor
No motion that pulls attention off the road

approach.d: Speed and warnings in the first level, at a size readable without focusing. Energy and route in the second. Everything else hidden until asked for.
Green for a healthy state only. No decorative green and no «brand» green — so when something turns amber or red the driver does not need to read why.
Contrast was measured under direct brightness, not on a desk monitor in a dark room. Anything that failed under the sun was redesigned.

cases.solution: A complete interface study in Figma with a three-level visual hierarchy, a semantic rather than decorative colour palette, and contrast measured under real lighting conditions.

impact.label: levels in the visual hierarchy
colour carrying the meaning of a healthy state
contrast tested under direct sun
motion that pulls attention off the road

notes.s: What must be seen in a fraction of a second, then what is read at a stop, then what is hidden.
Green for a healthy state only — so a change in colour means something really changed.
Contrast measured under direct brightness, not on a desk monitor in a dark room.

cases.title: Island Haven
cases.headline: a tech incubator whose numbers can be verified
cases.summary: An incubator platform in Gaza: every public number is cryptographically signed with Ed25519, and the visitor's own browser verifies it through WebCrypto — no trust in the server required.
cases.heroAlt: The verification page at Island Haven: a public Ed25519 key and three checks running in the browser — the hash matches, the signature is valid, the key is published

gallery.cap: The verification page — three checks running in the visitor's browser, not on our server

metric.honor: A cryptographic signature on every public number

challenge.p: An incubator publishing public numbers — companies, funding, graduates — in an environment where every number is doubted. What was needed was not «believe us», but «check for yourselves».
points: Every public number cryptographically signed and sealed in a hash chain
Verification running in the visitor's browser through WebCrypto — not through our server
Arabic first in direction, typography and numerals, with English as a layer above it
Content baked into the page source, readable before any JavaScript runs

approach.d: Public numbers are sealed in a hash chain and the public key is published. The verification page runs three checks in the visitor's browser: the hash matches, the signature is valid, the key is published.
The content is baked into the page source, so the visitor — and the search engine — reads before any JavaScript runs. JavaScript adds the verification; it does not carry the content.
Direction, typography and numerals are Arabic by origin, with English as a layer above — not the other way round. WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility across the platform.

cases.solution: A React platform with server-side rendering, an Ed25519 signature on every public number, and verification in the browser through WebCrypto. Trust never passes through us.

impact.label: verification checks running in the browser
trust required in the server
a cryptographic signature on every public number
WCAG 2.1 accessibility across the platform

notes.s: Public numbers are sealed in a hash chain and the key is published. Verification runs in the browser, so it never passes through us.
Direction, typography and numerals are Arabic by origin, with English as a layer above — not the other way round.
The content is baked into the page source, so the visitor reads before any JavaScript runs.
